info.title: Micropod API · SandboxService
info.description:
## micropod.v1.SandboxService

Sandboxes as a programmable environment: boot a micro-VM once, then run
 processes in it, stream their output, move files in and out, and watch
 paths — the surface the SDKs' `Sandbox` class is built on.

 A sandbox is a `runtime: sandbox` container owned by the API process; every
 call names it by container id. Processes and file operations run inside
 the container, seeing its mounts, /tmp and working directory. File
 operations and the idle main process use /bin/sh and the usual tools
 (busybox or coreutils), so distroless images can run processes but not
 file operations.

post.description:
Save the sandbox's disk as a checkpoint, then stop the sandbox. Boot a
 new one from it with StartSandboxRequest.from_checkpoint.
Copy a file, or a directory tree with `recursive`.
Checkpoints saved on this host (shared with `micropod sandbox checkpoint`).
Create a directory (with parents unless `recursive` is false).
A file's bytes, up to 32 MiB.
Delete a file, or a directory — non-empty ones only with `recursive`.
Move a path; atomic within one filesystem.

Start a process in a running sandbox; returns at once with its id.
 Follow it with StreamProcess.

Boot a sandbox and return once it can take processes. With no `command`
 it idles until stopped (DeleteContainer) — the long-lived shape the SDKs
 use.

Metadata for a path, not following a final symlink; `not_found` when the
 path does not exist.

The process's stdout and stderr as they arrive, then its exit. Output
 from before the stream opened is replayed first (up to 8 MiB), so
 start-then-stream never loses a byte; several streams may follow one
 process. A stream that falls too far behind fails with
 `resource_exhausted` instead of silently dropping output.

Changes under a path, observed inside the guest — including writes a
 host-side watcher never sees (the root disk, tmpfs, overlay mounts).
 Uses inotify when the image has inotifywait (inotify-tools), otherwise
 polls every 500 ms at one-second mtime resolution. The first event is
 "ready": changes after it are reported.
Create or replace a file (or append to it), up to 32 MiB per call.

Write to the process's stdin (StartProcessRequest.stdin); `close` sends
 EOF after the data.

connect-protocol-version.title: Connect-Protocol-Version
connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is no limit on the number of messages.

type.description: A URL that acts as a globally unique identifier for the type of the serialized message. For example: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo`. This is used to determine the schema of the data in the `value` field and is the discriminator for the `debug` field.

value.description: The Protobuf message, serialized as bytes and base64-encoded. The specific message type is identified by the `type` field.

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Deserialized error detail payload. The 'type' field indicates the schema. This field is for easier debugging and should not be relied upon for application logic.

connect.error_details.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message, with an additional debug field for ConnectRPC error details.

name.title: name
name.description: Checkpoint name; an existing one is replaced.

id.title: id
id.description: Container ID — `container` uses the user-assigned name as the ID.

micropod.v1.ContainerRef.title: ContainerRef
micropod.v1.ContainerRef.description: Reference to an existing container (or the ID returned by run/create).

micropod.v1.Empty.title: Empty
micropod.v1.Empty.description:
The Micropod daemon API is grouped into per-domain services, one per file:

   container.proto — ContainerService (lifecycle, logs, stats, exec)
   image.proto     — ImageService (list, pull, delete)
   volume.proto    — VolumeService (volumes + mount policy)
   network.proto   — NetworkService
   compose.proto   — Compose (up/down over a compose spec)
   system.proto    — SystemService (snapshot, usage, app updates)

 Empty is shared by every service, so it lives here.

mtime.title: mtime
mtime.description: Last modification, seconds since the epoch.

micropod.v1.PathRequest.title: PathRequest
micropod.v1.PathRequest.description: A path inside a sandbox; relative paths resolve against its workdir.

hostIp.title: host_ip
hostIp.description: Host interface IP to bind (empty = all interfaces).

micropod.v1.PortMapping.title: PortMapping
micropod.v1.PortMapping.description: A published port mapping between host and container.

exitCode.title: exit_code
exitCode.description: The last event: the exit code (128 + n when killed by signal n).

stderr.title: stderr
stderr.description: Bytes the process wrote to stderr.

stdout.title: stdout
stdout.description: Bytes the process wrote to stdout.

micropod.v1.ProcessEvent.title: ProcessEvent
micropod.v1.ProcessEvent.description: One piece of a process's life, in order: output chunks, then its exit.

micropod.v1.ProcessRef.title: ProcessRef
micropod.v1.ProcessRef.description: A process in a sandbox. `pid` is set in StartProcess's response.

recursive.title: recursive
recursive.description: Required to delete a non-empty directory.

image.title: image
image.description: The image the checkpoint's disk was first built from.

sizeBytes.title: size_bytes
sizeBytes.description: Bytes allocated on the host (clones share blocks, so often less).

mode.title: mode
mode.description:
"overlay" (default): guest writes go to a per-sandbox copy and the host
 directory is untouched. "ro": read-only. "rw": guest writes reach the
 host directory.

micropod.v1.SandboxMount.title: SandboxMount
micropod.v1.SandboxMount.description: A host directory shared into the sandbox.

exposeHost.title: expose_host
exposeHost.description:
Host loopback ports the guest reaches as host.micropod.internal:<port>
 (e.g. a database on the host). Nothing else on the host is reachable.

allowHosts.title: allow_hosts
allowHosts.description:
Egress allowlist. When set, the VM has no route out of its own: all
 traffic leaves through a host proxy that refuses every other host.
 "*.example.com" matches subdomains only. Needs a network.

secrets.title: secrets
secrets.description:
Secrets by the environment variable name the guest sees. The guest gets
 a random placeholder; the host proxy swaps in the real value only in the
 request line and headers of HTTPS requests to the secret's `hosts`, so
 the credential never enters the VM. Needs a network.

dnsResolvers.title: dns_resolvers
dnsResolvers.description: Guest nameservers (default: the network gateway). Needs a network.

diskSizeMib.title: disk_size_mib
diskSizeMib.description: Root disk size in MiB for image bases (0 = the default, 8192).

micropod.v1.SandboxOptions.title: SandboxOptions
micropod.v1.SandboxOptions.description:
What a sandbox may reach beyond its own VM, and the credentials it may use
 without seeing them.

value.title: value
value.description:
The real value. SDKs read `from` environment variables on the caller's
 side and send the value here.

command.title: command
command.description:
Or an argv run on the host (no shell) whose stdout is the value — raw,
 or {"version":1,"value":"…","expires_at":"<RFC 3339>"} like AWS
 `credential_process`. Minted on first use, again a minute before
 `expires_at` (else every `ttl`), one run at a time, kept in memory only.
 A failed refresh keeps a still-valid value; with none, requests to
 `hosts` fail closed (502) instead of carrying the placeholder upstream.

commandDir.title: command_dir
commandDir.description: Working directory for `command` (default: the API process's home).

ttl.title: ttl
ttl.description:
Refresh interval when `command` reports no expiry, e.g. "15m", "1h",
 "90s" (default 5m).

hosts.title: hosts
hosts.description:
HTTPS hosts whose requests get the real value ("*.example.com" matches
 subdomains).

micropod.v1.SandboxSecret.title: SandboxSecret
micropod.v1.SandboxSecret.description:
One secret: a value the caller already has, or a host command that mints
 it (and mints it again before it expires).
sandbox_secret.source // set exactly one of value or command

command.title: command
command.description: argv; use ["sh", "-c", "…"] for a shell line.

stdin.title: stdin
stdin.description: Keep stdin open for WriteProcessStdin; otherwise the process reads EOF.

fromCheckpoint.title: from_checkpoint
fromCheckpoint.description:
Or a checkpoint saved by CheckpointSandbox or `micropod sandbox
 checkpoint create`.

name.title: name
name.description: Optional name; becomes the sandbox (container) id.

env.title: env
env.description: KEY=VALUE environment for the sandbox and every process started in it.

ports.title: ports
ports.description: TCP ports to publish; an empty host_ip binds 127.0.0.1.

allowNet.title: allow_net
allowNet.description:
A NAT network with internet access (default off: no network device
 unless ports or expose_host need a host-only one).

options.title: options
options.description: Host ports, egress allowlist, secrets, DNS, disk size.

command.title: command
command.description: Main process; empty idles until the sandbox is stopped.

micropod.v1.StartSandboxRequest.title: StartSandboxRequest
micropod.v1.StartSandboxRequest.description: start_sandbox.base // set image or from_checkpoint, not both

event.title: event
event.description:
"ready" (first, once the watch is live), then "create", "modify",
 "delete" or "rename" (both ends of a move, with inotify).

path.title: path
path.description: Absolute guest path of what changed.
